answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to a licensed pearl-diving season on one named reef. An independent marine registrar weighs and seals every pearl the diver brings up, while a walnut-wood float rides the zephyr above the reef as the diver's surface marker. Random checks summon the diver to surface live from that exact reef within minutes, so one operator cannot dive two reefs at once. The license fee in outside money doubles per further identity on the same funding trail, so each extra fake costs another reef lease, another diving season, another human, and twice the prior fee.
